tag: the serial path stops being the default
why: L1. A sharded run is proven equivalent on ONE list on ONE machine, which is evidence about that run and not a promotion. Making it the default means every round's central verification silently moves to the experimental path, and the first time a copy is imperfect or a shard is lost the round still reports a verdict — a smaller, greener one.

tag: the serial branch is removed, so there is no trusted path to compare against
new: rep = sweep_sharded(blinds, a.tests, a.store, max(2, a.shards))
why: L1, the other direction. Equivalence was established by running BOTH on the same list and comparing verdicts; delete the serial path and that comparison can never be repeated, so the claim becomes unfalsifiable — which is the exact article this harness exists to serve.

old:
for i, b in enumerate(blinds):
        buckets[i % len(buckets)].append(b)
new:
for i, b in enumerate(blinds[:-1] if len(blinds) > 1 else blinds):
        buckets[i % len(buckets)].append(b)
why: L2, and it is the defect this harness exists to catch committed INSIDE the harness: a sweep that quietly loses one blind reports a shorter, greener list and nothing about the output says a blind is missing. The leg partitions 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 10 and 36 blinds across 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 shards and reconciles every tag, because an off-by-one in a partition hides at most sizes.

tag: the partition becomes unbalanced, wasting the parallelism it bought
new:
buckets[0].extend(blinds)
    return [b for b in buckets if b]
why: L2. Everything in one bucket loses no blind and reports every verdict correctly — it just takes exactly as long as the serial path while claiming to be sharded. That is a performance claim with no mechanism behind it, and the measured 1.60x would silently become 1.0x with nothing in the output changing.

tag: a shard stops proving it imports its own copy
why: L3, THE HAZARD THAT DECIDES WHETHER ANY OF THIS IS SAFE. A stray jules_ai.pth puts the real repo root on sys.path for every local process, so a shard can import the ORIGINAL agentic_core while mutating its own copy — and then every verdict it reports is about a tree nobody is committing. PYTHONPATH is MEASURED to win over the .pth, but 'should win' is not a measurement, and this is the assertion that makes it one.

tag: the merge stops reconciling its results against the blind list
why: L4. A lost shard and a double-counted one look nothing alike and both read as success without this: the first gives a shorter greener list, the second inflates a count. My own memory of this programme records a refutation run where a slice() cap dropped findings silently — count findings against verdicts, always.

tag: a shard reporting fewer blinds than it was given is accepted
new: if False and len(r.get("results") or []) != n_expected:
why: L4. This is the per-shard half of the same property and it catches a different failure: a shard that crashed halfway writes a VALID report containing only the blinds it reached. The merge-level check would then compare a short list against a short list and agree with itself.

tag: the sharded path stops proving it left the real tree alone
old:
if now != sha:
            raise RuntimeError(f"THE REAL TREE WAS MUTATED by a sharded sweep: {f} {sha} -> {now}")
why: L5, and it is the sharded path's whole safety claim rather than a nicety. The one mutation that ever survived a kill in this programme survived it in the real tree; a sharded run has nothing there to survive, and this check is what turns that from a design intention into a verified fact after every run.

tag: the in-flight refusal blocks a sharded run that cannot leave a marker
why: L5. The marker is a SERIAL-path safeguard: it names a real-tree file and the sha to restore it to. A sharded run never mutates the real tree, so a stale marker left by a killed serial run would block the one path that cannot possibly have caused it — a safeguard refusing the thing it protects.

tag: clause (b) claims the row's projected speedup instead of the measured one
why: The bar must carry the figure that was measured, not the one that was hoped for. 4 shards came out WORSE than 2 (211s against 162s) because contention, not the single tree, is the limit on 6 cores and 8.3 GB — and a bar quoting 3.2x would send a later round hunting for a speedup that does not exist on this machine at any shard count.
